metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

metadata.source: OIDC authorization endpoint documented generically; included as shared infrastructure per instructions, though not specific to SAML app acting as IdP.
OIDC token endpoint documented in SDK conventions and application data structure.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to an existing account when the email matches.
saml.note: Cross-protocol or cross-connector account merge on matching email is documented behavior and should not be reported as an identity collision by itself.

saml.description: Transient Name ID format generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Different downstream identifiers across repeated logins are expected when Transient NameID is configured.

saml.description: Persistent and Unspecified Name ID formats use the Logto user ID as the NameID.
saml.note: Downstream NameID may differ from email or username because Logto uses its internal user ID by design.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL.
saml.note: This can look like premature refresh-token expiry but is documented session binding behavior.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Use userinfo or introspection for verification; lack of JWT claims in the token itself is by design.

saml.description: Administrator password updates via Management API are exempt from the current password policy.
saml.note: Weak passwords set by admins do not imply end-user password-policy enforcement is broken.

saml.description: Admins can create users with blocked or subaddressed emails via Console or Management API even when end-user blocklist rules would reject them.
saml.note: Admin provisioning bypass of end-user blocklist restrictions is documented behavior and should not be reported as a sign-up bypass.

saml.constraint: SAML in Logto is IdP mode for SAML applications, not a documented SAML Assertion Consumer Service endpoint on Logto itself. Do NOT attempt upstream `saml_login` attacks against Logto as an SP from these docs; the provided documentation only covers configuring Logto to issue SAML responses to downstream service providers.

For I4 tests involving enterprise SSO account binding, Logto documentation states that SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. Treat same-email merge across SSO and existing accounts as BY DESIGN, not as an identity-collision vulnerability.

For SAML NameID binding tests, the default Name ID format is Persistent and uses the Logto user ID as NameID. If you need email-based downstream identity behavior, you MUST explicitly configure the SAML application Name ID format to Email address; otherwise tests assuming email NameID will be invalid.

For SAML privacy / principal-binding tests, Transient Name ID intentionally generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request. Do NOT flag changing NameID values as replay or identity-binding bugs when Name ID format is configured as Transient.

For SAML assertion confidentiality tests, enabling assertion encryption requires providing the SP certificate. Do NOT interpret failures after enabling encryption without a certificate as security enforcement bugs; the configuration is incomplete by design.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. For any I5 token-exchange scenario, you MUST first enable the application's 'Allow token exchange' setting; otherwise rejection is expected and not evidence of audience/scope enforcement.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, use the OAuth token endpoint `/oidc/token` with `resource` as the audience parameter. Logto documentation binds exchanged access tokens to the specified resource; tests must vary `resource` explicitly rather than assuming implicit audience selection.

For I2 refresh-token/session lifetime interpretation, a refresh token issued without `offline_access` is session-bound and the user session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. Do NOT treat refresh-token invalidation after session expiry as an independent refresh-token TTL bug.

Numeric sentinel analysis: refresh token rotation has threshold semantics, not simple boolean freshness. When enabled, Logto issues a new refresh token if rotation age reaches one year, if >=70% of original TTL has passed, or always for public clients. Do NOT assume every refresh request rotates for confidential clients.

Numeric sentinel analysis: opaque token and example access token lifetime is documented as `expires_in: 3600`; SMS/email verification codes expire in 10 minutes and are not customizable. Use these documented fixed lifetimes as platform behavior and do not search for undocumented TTL configuration sentinels in SAML tests.

For I3 config-change tests involving signing keys, Cloud tenants apply new signing keys immediately after rotation, but consecutive rotations can invalidate all issued tokens. A valid coherence test should perform a single rotation and compare pre/post behavior; do NOT rotate multiple times in one sequence.

For I3 config-change tests on OSS, signing-key rotation requires a Logto instance restart before the new key takes effect. Without restart, stale acceptance/rejection is expected operational behavior, not a cache-coherence vulnerability.

Redirect URI matching for applications supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname, not in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Tests that rely on redirect URI mismatch behavior must respect these wildcard semantics; otherwise failures may reflect valid wildcard matching rather than weak validation.

Because Logto supports wildcard redirect URIs for SPA and traditional web apps, redirect acceptance of preview-style subdomains may be by configuration. Do NOT flag wildcard-authorized redirects as open redirect bugs unless the accepted URI falls outside the configured wildcard rules.

SAML in the provided Logto docs is Logto-as-IdP for SAML applications, not Logto-as-SP consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML ACS-style saml_login tests against Logto from this documentation set; there is no documented SAML assertion consumer endpoint here for broker-side SAML login.

For SAML protocol runs on Logto, test setup must use Management API/admin operations plus downstream OIDC inspection endpoints where documented. The docs do not provide a documented SAML login API or password login API for admin automation in this corpus; treat login_with_password and saml_login as absent from the documented API surface for this protocol run.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

When testing I5 token-exchange scope escalation, always include a control exchange with the original intended scope/resource. Expanded-scope failures may simply reflect application configuration or disabled permissions, not correct authorization binding. Compare exchanged token scope/claims against the original authorization intent.

For token_exchange tests, audience/resource binding is expressed with OAuth token endpoint parameters such as resource and possibly audience depending on client flow. The docs explicitly show resource for exchanged access tokens; use the resource parameter as the primary authorization target and do not assume arbitrary audience values are accepted unless the application is configured for them.

Opaque vs JWT access token behavior is context-dependent in Logto. If no resource or organization is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. For verification and I2/I5 tests, choose the correct verifier: use /oidc/me for opaque OP tokens and /oidc/token/introspection when token format is opaque or when claims must be server-validated.

Refresh-token/session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, which has a fixed TTL of 14 days. Tests that expect refresh-token lifetime to follow configured refresh-token TTL MUST request offline_access, otherwise expiry may be caused by session expiration rather than token TTL.

Refresh token rotation is enabled by default and public clients receive a new refresh token on refresh when rotation is enabled. I2 replay/freshness tests involving refresh tokens MUST track the latest refresh token value after each successful refresh; reusing an older rotated token may fail by design.

Management API user creation requires at least one identifier among primaryEmail, primaryPhone, or username. Test setup that creates users for SAML/email-binding scenarios MUST provide at least one such identifier or creation will fail for non-security reasons.

Enterprise SSO account linking is by email match: adding SSO links identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 collision tests involving SAML/enterprise identities, email-based merges are BY DESIGN and must not be flagged as identity-collision vulnerabilities unless the merge violates documented email ownership/verification assumptions.

Only verified email or phone values from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail or primaryPhone. I4 tests that rely on unverified upstream attributes becoming primary identifiers will produce false positives; use verified attributes when testing account-linking or principal-binding behavior.

Username case sensitivity is deployment-configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME and defaults to true. For I4 case-confusion tests, do not assume case-insensitive username normalization; determine deployment setting first or restrict collision tests to email/SSO identifiers documented for the flow.
For OIDC userinfo verification, the endpoint is /oidc/me, not /userinfo. Use the documented Logto path exactly; otherwise verification failures are harness errors, not auth failures.

SAML in Logto docs is IdP mode for SAML applications, not an upstream SAML broker login API. Do NOT attempt to extract or call a documented ACS endpoint for broker-side saml_login from these docs; the documented SAML flow is your application sending AuthnRequest to Logto and receiving a SAML response from Logto.

For SAML-profile testing on Logto, use Management API application creation/update to configure a SAML application (ACS URL / Reply URL and SP Entity ID). The docs do not expose a REST SAML callback endpoint for forged upstream assertions, so saml_login is absent from the documented API surface for this protocol run.

Enterprise SSO account linking is BY EMAIL MATCH. Documentation states SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise identities, email collisions can intentionally merge identities; do NOT treat same-email linking as a bug without evidence that distinct emails or intended-separate accounts were merged.

For I4 cross-protocol or SAML email-binding tests, only VERIFIED email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail. If the upstream email is unverified, primaryEmail may remain unset; do not interpret missing email sync as failed binding logic.

NameID format is configurable on SAML applications. Default is Persistent, which uses the Logto user ID as NameID; Email address uses the user's email; Transient generates a one-time identifier; Unspecified currently also uses Logto user ID. I4 identity comparisons must account for the configured NameID format rather than assuming NameID equals email or username.

Transient NameID is BY DESIGN one-time and changes with each authentication request. Do NOT flag changing NameID values across repeated SAML logins as an I4 principal-binding bug when the SAML app is configured with Transient Name ID format.

Applications must explicitly enable token exchange. Token exchange is disabled by default; if not enabled in application settings, /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange will fail with 'token exchange is not allowed for this application'. Any I5 token-exchange test MUST first enable Allow token exchange on the application.

Refresh token/session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After the session expires, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. For lifetime-sensitive tests, include offline_access if you need the configured refresh-token TTL to take effect.

Rotate refresh token behavior is special for public clients (SPA/native): when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh-token exchange. Tests that compare token reuse or stale refresh-token behavior must account for rotation rather than assuming stable refresh tokens.

Redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For flow-coherence tests, do not assume exact-match-only redirect URI validation if the application type permits wildcard redirect URIs.

User search parameter semantics: search and search.<field> support configurable matching modes via mode / mode.<field>. Available modes are exact, like, similar_to, and posix. Because matching mode is explicit, do not assume wildcard '*' semantics; use the documented mode controls. For I4 multi-identity lookups, exact mode is safest when you need deterministic equality rather than fuzzy matching.

User search is case-insensitive by default unless isCaseSensitive=true. For I4 case-confusion tests (e.g., 'Admin' vs 'admin'), you MUST run both a case-insensitive lookup baseline and a case-sensitive lookup, otherwise search results may collapse by design and create false positives.

Fuzzy search modes (like, similar_to, posix) only support matching one value per field. If you need to match multiple candidate values for a single field in I4 collision tests, use mode.<field>=exact and repeat search.<field> parameters; otherwise the search behavior is not equivalent.

Management API user creation and password reset can bypass password policy checks. Docs state PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt from password policy enforcement. Do NOT use admin-set passwords as evidence that weak-password acceptance exists in end-user authentication flows.

Blocklist restrictions and some sign-up restrictions can be bypassed by admins via Console or Management API user creation. If a blocked email or subaddressed email can be created through admin APIs, that is BY DESIGN and not an authentication bypass in end-user flows.

Refresh token TTL default/sentinel semantics from docs: default refresh token TTL is 14 days for non-SPA apps; SPA does not support TTL refreshment through token requests. Do not assume token refresh extends TTL on SPA clients.
